NATS wins when you need both pub/sub AND request-reply in the same broker — its subject hierarchy is more expressive and JetStream gives you persistence — but it costs ~30MB of resident memory which matters on the tightest devices. Pick MQTT if pub/sub alone is sufficient and memory is tight; pick NATS when the workload needs request-reply or you have >256MB RAM to spare. The full research artifact (actors, integration points, decision criteria) is captured in the chain entity for follow-up.
